newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire house votes Rwanda, Burundi, Uganda break.
newsitem.headline: Zaire house votes Rwanda, Burundi, Uganda break.

text.p: Zaire's transitional parliament has voted to sever diplomatic relations with Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda, three neighbours accused by the government of waging war against the sprawling Central African nation.

State radio reported on Friday that the assembly voted overwhelmingly in favour of the move at the end of a marathon debate. It was not immediately clear when the move, approved late on Thursday, would formally take effect.
Zaire has accused Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda of waging war against it in its volatile eastern refugee zone where hard-pressed Zairean troops are battling ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels.

In Nairobi, a Kenyan official said a summit of at least seven African states in Kenya on November 5 would focus on the war in eastern Zaire. David Kikaya of the foreign ministry said Kenya had invited Zaire but had no official response yet.
Earlier, Zaire defiantly rejected peace talks with its neighbours despite fears that rebel victories could herald its disintegration.

"The government will not undertake any negotiation, will not participate in any regional conference while a part of national territory is occupied by foreign forces," Zairean Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo told Thursday's emergency session.

"This war which the combined forces of Uganda, Burundi and Rwanda are waging against Zaire has brought to broad daylight Rwanda's intention not to welcome on its territory its nationals living in Zaire and to pursue its insane plan of annexing a part of our territory."
